correctness.rationale: Solved inhomogeneous recurrence b_n=2u_n where u_n=A lambda^n+B lambda^(−n)−1/4 in Q_p[sqrt2] with A=(sqrt2−1)/(8sqrt2), B=(sqrt2+1)/(8sqrt2). Squaring yields 5 distinct spectral bases lambda^j for j=−2,−1,0,1,2 with constant coefficient 5/64. Unit norms N(lambda−1)=−4, N(lambda+1)=8, N(lambda²+lambda+1)=49, N(lambda²+1)=36 rule out eigenvalue collisions for p>=5 except7, so the five-window Vandermonde is invertible over Z_p[sqrt2]. Every window divisible by p^e iff both p^e|5k and lambda^k≡1 mod p^e; the factors four from b_n=2u_n do not change good-prime valuations. d_p divides p−(2/p) and p∤d_p; odd-prime binomial lifting gives val(lambda^(d_p)-1)+vp(k), truncated by 5k. At p=5, lambda^3=99+70sqrt2, lambda^6=19601+13860sqrt2 gives d5=6 and initial valuation 1. Independent integer-recursion + gcd of five consecutive windows + modular norm-one order verification compared 1,848 valuations for 84 k and 22 eligible primes p<100. The finite check is corroboration.
